citations.quote: Our analysis implies that what is relevant to investment is marginal q the ratio of the market value of a marginal unit of capital to its replacement cost.
In Section 9.8, we will consider adjustment costs that take more complicated forms than the smooth adjustment costs of q theory.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Romer Ch.9 q-theory of investment: static firm-profit-max extended to dynamic neoclassical investment with quadratic adjustment costs; Tobin's q = 1 at steady state; user cost of capital P_K(r + δ − π̇_K/P_K) as the threshold rental rate.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Investment with Adjustment Costs and Tobin's q
